text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP for a weekend. Prices below come from the reviews and may have changed.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 290Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**: best overall pick at ~$249. It has 288Wh, weighs 8.3 lb and is simple to use. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you'll find the Plus at Amazon and other retailers. [PowerStationGearLab review and buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**: best value at ~$269-299. It has 286Wh and a 600W inverter (double the Jackery's), and it can expand to 572Wh. Same page as above.
- **Anker SOLIX C300**: ~$199 with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet model, not the "C300 DC."
- **Bluetti EB3A**: the budget pick at ~$179, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter.

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge or power tools
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 16 kg (~35 lb), $499. With code AFF5OFF it's **$474.05** at Bluetti's official US store, a code Dealectric tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. It has a 5-year warranty and can't be expanded. The $599 listing is a bundle with a 100W solar panel. [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link; Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you, and Bluetti's checkout has the final word on price).
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb and was reported under $900 on Amazon, against a $1,499 list price. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, reported under $530 on sale. It's compact but has limited capacity (890Wh measured), and the fan is noisy. Same page as above.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's camping pick at about $1,079. It's IP65-rated, has 1,536Wh, and comes with a 5-year warranty. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Tips
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the draw, and a 288Wh unit then covers 3-5 nights.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge at camp. Jackery panels pair most easily with Jackery stations.
- Power stations exceed the 100Wh airline limit, so they're for car and campsite use only.

If you tell me your trip length and what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, etc.), I can narrow this to one pick.
